name: Blood Pact lets its caster dodge or parry while casting (#3245)
contract: Blood Pact 801955's tooltip closing clause promises its caster can still dodge or parry while casting. Unit::CanDefendDuringCast() gates that at the 4 dodge/parry call sites in Unit.cpp that otherwise zero dodge/parry chance through IsNonMeleeSpellCast's generic-cast branch. QA Test 100% Dodge 10020 (aura 49 SPELL_AURA_MOD_DODGE_PERCENT, EffectBasePoints 99 + DieSides 1 = 100) plus Evasion 5277 (same aura, EffectBasePoints 49 + DieSides 1 = 50) are both applied as a fixture, past the 10000/10000 roll ceiling Unit::RollMeleeOutcomeAgainst compares dodge_chance*100 against, so every swing that is actually rolled is a certain dodge, independent of the fix under test. The attacker's melee_hit_rating removes misses so every swing that is NOT dodged lands; the attacker deliberately carries no expertise_rating, since RollMeleeOutcomeAgainst subtracts Player::GetExpertiseDodgeOrParryReduction from dodge_chance before the cast check runs, which would cancel the fixture regardless of the fix (this is why an earlier statistical attempt at this regression, recorded in bloodmage-blood-pact.json's prior contract text, saw landed rates far above what a dodge fixture should allow). Bloodmoon Blast 572332 is a real 2000 ms Bloodmage cast (confirmed by spell_cast_time_ms). A player's very first native autoattack (its own attack timer still at its initial zero) delivers its first swing almost immediately on the attack request rather than waiting a full weapon-swing cycle; a later swing, or a swing after stop_attack/attack on the same player, waits out the rest of the normal weapon-swing cycle, which is longer than this 2000 ms cast. Each phase therefore issues its cast first and only then sends a player's own first-ever attack request, making that one guaranteed instant first swing the swing under measurement, provably mid-cast rather than racing the cast's own registration into m_currentSpells or landing in an idle gap between casts. The test phase uses a second, otherwise identical attacker player for exactly this reason: it has never attacked before, so its own first attack request reproduces the same instant swing the control phase observed on the first attacker. The swing/damage snapshots are taken between the cast and the attack request, and the 500 ms wait afterwards (with an explicit casting==1 check) stays inside the 2000 ms cast. Control: without Blood Pact, IsNonMeleeSpellCast's generic-cast branch zeros the 100% dodge while casting, so every mid-cast swing lands (melee_damage_count tracks melee_attack_count 1:1). Test: with Blood Pact learned and active, CanDefendDuringCast() keeps the 100% dodge fixture live during the same kind of cast, so every mid-cast swing is dodged (melee_damage_count stays at 0) even though the attacker keeps swinging. Blood Pact's own native effects (its own +50 dodge, the ranged-hit debuff, the Blood Runs Cold healing clause) are covered by bloodmage-blood-pact.json and are not re-exercised here; the 100% dodge comes only from the QA fixture, isolating the cast-defense mechanism from the spell's own magnitude.
